answer: Sybil resistance here is a bonded, correlated-identity slash. Each agent locks a stake that is listed in a public atlas of operators, so cheap throwaway names have a real cost. Fresh identities may dock only at a scheduled jetty, where already-bonded peers must countersign. A signature is void if the attestor and applicant share a training-run, custody, or key-derivation ridge; detected clusters forfeit every locked bond. Farming many personas then requires uncorrelated attestors and repeated stake, which usually costs more than stuffing a vote can return.
